data.name: Amir
data.gender_notes: Amir is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Amir is an Arabic name meaning 'commander', 'leader', or 'prince'. It denotes one who has authority and is respected for his wisdom, fairness, and leadership. It is a title historically used for rulers and respected Islamic figures. The name Amir carries the meaning “Prince, Leader, Commander” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in English, Urdu, Arabic. Parents who choose Amir usually hope their child will grow to embody prince, leader, commander and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Amir reflects a personality that leads with grace and justice — a soul destined for influence, guidance, and honor.
data.etymology: Amir belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Prince, Leader, Commander.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amir total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_arabic.name: أَمِير
in_arabic.long_meaning: أَمِير: يأتي من الأَميرُ، الذي هو مُشتق من الكَلِمِ الأَرَبيّ الْأَمَرُ، الَّذي يَعني النّزاع، الرّأي، الحَكم، المُلك، السّلطان، الَّذي يُعتَبَر في الْإِسلامِ كَمُصطلَحٍ رُبّانِيٍّ، يُشَمِل مَن يَحوزُ السُلطانَ، وَيُفدى العَامةَ، وَيُحَيى الحُقوقُ، وَيُحَفظَ العِدلُ

in_urdu.name: امیر
in_urdu.meaning: امیر کوڑا، فہم، حکومت، بادشاہت، سلطنت

in_hindi.name: आमीर

in_english.name: Amir
in_english.long_meaning: Amir is an Arabic name meaning commander, leader, ruler, monarch, sovereignty, and is used in Islamic tradition to refer to a great person or king who exercises authority over others. The name Amir is derived from the Arabic root 'amr', which means power, authority, and command. In Islamic history, Amir was used as a title for rulers and leaders who were known for their wisdom, justice, and leadership qualities.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Amir" holds a significant importance in Islamic culture, as it is often associated with royalty, power, and leadership. In Islamic history, many great leaders and conquerors were known as Amirs, such as Saladin and Sultan Mehmed II. The name conveys a sense of strength, dignity, and power that is greatly valued in Islamic society.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, an Amir is not just someone who wields power, but someone who uses that power to serve and protect others. In Islamic tradition, a true Amir is someone who embodies wisdom, fairness, and compassion, and leads his people with justice and righteousness. The Prophet Muhammad said, "The best of you are those who have the best manners and character" (Bukhari), illustrating the spiritual qualities that an Amir should strive to cultivate in himself. Therefore, the name "Amir" carries deeper spiritual significance as a reminder to use power and influence for the greater good, in line with Islamic values of service to others and the pursuit of knowledge and wisdom.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Amir: Commander of the faithful, a leader guiding his community towards righteousness and spiritual growth.
